48.why: Isobaric: constant pressure; isothermal: constant temperature; adiabatic: no heat exchange; isochoric: constant volume.

49.why: The second law brings in entropy, the zeroth law defines thermal equilibrium, Gay-Lussac's law gives P ∝ T and the first law is energy conservation.

50.why: Molar Cv is 3/2 R for a monatomic gas, 5/2 R for a diatomic gas and 3 R for a non-linear polyatomic gas.

51.why: Heat is measured in joules, pressure in pascals, temperature in kelvin and entropy in J/K.

52.why: Isobaric: P constant; adiabatic: PV^γ constant; isochoric: V constant; isothermal: PV constant.

94.why: Velocity is in m/s, acceleration m/s², displacement m and jerk (rate of change of acceleration) m/s³.

95.why: Uniform motion has constant velocity, uniformly accelerated motion constant acceleration, projectiles follow a parabola, circular motion has centripetal acceleration and free fall has acceleration g.

96.why: The three equations of motion give final velocity, displacement and the velocity-displacement relation; the last two give a projectile's range and maximum height.

139.why: R is the gas constant, M the molar mass, k Boltzmann's constant and Nₐ Avogadro's number.

140.why: A monatomic gas has 3, a rigid diatomic 5, a vibrating diatomic 7 and a non-linear triatomic 6 degrees of freedom.

141.why: Gay-Lussac's law holds volume constant, Boyle's law temperature, Charles's law pressure, and Avogadro's law compares gases at the same P, V and T.

171.why: The first law is the law of inertia, momentum stays constant without external force, the second law is F = dp/dt and the third law pairs action and reaction.

172.why: Kinetic friction is roughly constant, static friction adjusts itself, limiting friction is the maximum static value and rolling friction is the smallest.

173.why: Momentum is in kg m/s, the coefficient of friction has no unit, force is in newtons and impulse in N s.

174.why: Gravity provides centripetal force for planets, dusting a carpet shows inertia of rest, mud flying off a wheel inertia of direction and a runner pushing back on the ground Newton's third law.

175.why: The normal force is perpendicular to the surface, friction opposes motion, tension pulls and gravity attracts.

203.why: L = Iω, τ = r × F, α = dω/dt and I = Σmr².

204.why: Solid sphere 2/5 MR², ring MR², hollow sphere 2/3 MR², disc 1/2 MR².

205.why: Force ↔ torque, momentum ↔ angular momentum, mass ↔ moment of inertia, velocity ↔ angular velocity.

206.why: The perpendicular axis theorem gives Iz = Ix + Iy, the radius of gyration is k = √(I/M) and the parallel axis theorem gives I = Icm + Md².

207.why: Rotational KE = ½Iω², translational KE = ½mv² and a rolling body has both.

219.why: Amplitude is maximum displacement, frequency oscillations per second, damping the fall in amplitude, the period the time for one oscillation and resonance maximum amplitude at the natural frequency.

253.why: Bulk modulus is volume stress/strain, Young's modulus longitudinal stress/strain, Poisson's ratio lateral/longitudinal strain and rigidity modulus shear stress/strain.

254.why: Real fluids have viscosity, ideal fluids none; turbulent flow is chaotic and streamline flow moves in smooth layers.

256.why: Pressure is in N/m², surface tension in N/m, strain has no unit and viscosity is in Pa s.

257.why: Bernoulli's theorem is about fluid flow, Hooke's law elasticity, Pascal's law pressure in fluids and Stokes' law viscous force.

291.why: Energy is the capacity to do work, work is force × displacement and power is work done per unit time.

332.why: Isobaric: constant pressure; adiabatic: no heat exchange; isothermal: constant temperature; isochoric: constant volume.

333.why: Zeroth law – thermal equilibrium; first – energy conservation; second – entropy; third – absolute zero.

334.why: Temperature in kelvin, heat in joules, entropy in J/K and pressure in pascals.

335.why: γ is about 1.67 for monatomic, 1.40 for diatomic and 1.33 for polyatomic gases.
